name: agilix
description: Run your dog-sport club, classes, seminars and dogs in Agilix from chat.

interface.longDescription: Agilix is the platform dog-sport clubs (agility, hoopers, nosework, obedience, FCI Rally Obedience, dog dancing) use to run training classes, venues, members, seminars and competitions. Connected to ChatGPT, club admins and trainers plan a class or a whole recurring schedule, invite members or groups, change or cancel classes, run the class roster and waiting list, schedule messages to participants, keep agenda and training notes and schedule when classes go public. Full club admins also run the club itself: its details and terms, the team, join requests and members, rates, dues, punch cards, venues, opening hours and rentals, and read the club's stats and payment history. Handlers add and update their dogs, change their profile and settings, see their payments, dues and training stats, sign their dogs up for classes or waiting lists, rent a training space, review clubs, find competitions in every sport and start a new club. Handlers also find seminars by place, date and topic, sign a dog up by day or by group, and read their seminar entries, fees and group schedule; seminar organizers and their co-organizers accept, reject and waitlist entries and build and publish each day's groups. On competition day ChatGPT tells a handler when their dog runs, reads the competition news and their dogs' ZKwP ranking points. Anyone can ask a rules question and get quoted passages from the FCI and ZKwP rulebooks with a link to the source, suggest a missing agility competition, and browse their own and public courses from the Agilix course designer. ChatGPT always asks for the missing details and shows a summary before anything is changed. Payments, photos and creating a seminar stay on agilix.dog: ChatGPT gives the link. What Agilix cannot do yet can be sent to the Agilix team as a feature request, only after the user says yes.
capabilities: Plan, change and cancel club classes
Run a class roster, waiting list and messages
Manage club settings, team, members and money
Manage venues, halls and opening hours
Look after your dogs, profile and payments
Find competitions and sign dogs up for classes
Find seminars, sign dogs up and run seminar entries
Answer rules questions with quotes from the rulebooks
Start times, competition news and ranking points
defaultPrompt: What classes are on in my club this week?
Create a beginners agility class next Tuesday at 18:00 for 6 dogs.
Which classes are my dogs signed up for this month?

positive.description: A club admin sees the coming week of classes
positive.prompt: What classes are on in my club called test over the next 7 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the upcoming classes of the club "test" with their dates and times. The club runs four weekly classes at Agilix Demo Hall, so the answer contains Hoopers Fun (Fridays 17:00), Obedience Basics (Saturdays 10:00), Puppy Foundations (Mondays 17:00) and Agility Beginners (Tuesdays 18:00). Nothing is changed.

positive.description: A club admin creates a class after confirming a summary
positive.prompt: In my club called test, create a class named Demo Agility next Wednesday at 19:00 in Hall A at Agilix Demo Hall, 60 minutes, 8 places.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT first shows a summary (club test, Agilix Demo Hall, Hall A, the date at 19:00, 60 minutes, Demo Agility, 8 places) and asks for confirmation; nothing is created yet. After the reply "yes" it creates the class and confirms it. If this case was already run for the same Wednesday, Hall A is taken at that time: ChatGPT then says the hall is busy and asks for another time or hall instead of creating a second class.

positive.description: A club admin cancels the next class of a weekly series
positive.prompt: Cancel the next Hoopers Fun class in my club called test.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT finds the next upcoming Hoopers Fun class (a weekly Friday 17:00 class in Hall B that runs until February 2027), names its date and asks for confirmation. After the reply "yes" it cancels that one class and confirms it. Later Hoopers Fun classes stay, so the case can be repeated.

positive.description: A handler sees the classes their dog is signed up for
positive.prompt: Which classes am I signed up for in the next two weeks?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the classes the signed-in user is signed up for with the dog "tester": Agility Beginners on Tuesdays at 18:00 and Obedience Basics on Saturdays at 10:00, both in the club "test" at Agilix Demo Hall. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: A club admin checks a venue's halls and opening hours
positive.prompt: What are the opening hours of Agilix Demo Hall in my club called test, and which halls does it have?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers that Agilix Demo Hall (Warszawa) has two halls, Hall A and Hall B, both open every day from 08:00 to 21:00. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: A handler reads the details of their own dog
positive.prompt: Show me everything Agilix has about my dog tester.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the signed-in user's only dog, "tester", and shows what its profile holds (name, breed, birth date, classes per sport and the other stored fields; empty fields are said to be empty). Nothing is changed.

positive.description: A trainer reads the roster of the next class
positive.prompt: Who is on the next Agility Beginners class in my club called test?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the next upcoming Agility Beginners class (weekly on Tuesdays at 18:00 in Hall A at Agilix Demo Hall), names its date and lists its participants: the signed-in user with the dog "tester", booked. Nothing is changed, so the case can be repeated.

positive.description: A full club admin sees which private classes could be scheduled to go public
positive.prompt: Which classes in my club called test are not public yet, and is any publishing scheduled?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the club's upcoming private classes (Hoopers Fun, Obedience Basics, Puppy Foundations and Agility Beginners) and says no publishing is scheduled. Nothing is scheduled without the user asking and confirming a summary.

positive.description: A full club admin reads the club's stats
positive.prompt: How is my club called test doing - how many classes did it run in recent months?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the club "test"'s figures per recent month: the number of classes, the minutes of training and how full the classes were. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: A full club admin reads the club team
positive.prompt: Who is on the team of my club called test?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the club "test"'s team: the signed-in user, its founder and full admin. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: A handler reads the details of a seminar they are signed up for
positive.prompt: Show me the details of the Agilix Demo Seminar I am signed up for - where and when is it, and which days can I still sign my dog up for?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds "Agilix Demo Seminar" among the signed-in user's entries, then shows its details: Warszawa, Agilix Demo Hall, 13 and 14 March 2027, sign-up by day with no approval needed, the dog "tester" already signed up for 13 March, 14 March still open, and a link to its page. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: A handler reads their own seminar entries
positive.prompt: Which seminars am I signed up for, and do I still owe anything?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the signed-in user's seminar entries: "Agilix Demo Seminar" in Warszawa with the dog "tester" on 13 March 2027, not on a waiting list, with no online fee to pay, and a link to the seminar page. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: A rules question is answered from the rulebooks
positive.prompt: In agility, how many refusals disqualify a dog from a run? Quote the rule.
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes at least one passage from an agility rulebook about refusals, naming the rulebook and its section, with a link to the rulebook file, and answers from that passage rather than from memory. Nothing is saved.

positive.description: A handler browses their own courses from the course designer
positive.prompt: Show me my courses in the Agilix course designer.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the signed-in user's course "Agilix Demo Jumping" (private, 10 jumps) with a link to open it in the Agilix course designer. Nothing is changed.

negative.description: Travel planning has nothing to do with club classes
negative.prompt: Find a dog-friendly hotel in Warsaw for next weekend.

negative.description: A weather question needs no club data
negative.prompt: What will the weather be in Warsaw this Saturday morning?

negative.description: A personal greeting needs no club data
negative.prompt: Write a short birthday message for my sister.

review.commerce_description: The app does not sell products or process payments. A class or training-space booking that must be paid ends with a link to pay on agilix.dog.

publication.release_notes: Club admins and trainers see who rented training spaces at their venue on given days, beside the classes held there, and a punch card entry is marked at the time of the class the user names, not only its day. Earlier: club management and full app parity: full club admins change the club's details, terms, team, members, groups, rates, dues, punch cards, venues and rentals, read the club's stats and payment history and schedule when classes go public; trainers run the class roster, attendance and waiting list, schedule messages to participants and keep agenda and training notes; handlers add, update and delete their dogs, change their profile and settings, see their payments, dues and stats, join class waiting lists, cancel their own rentals, review clubs, find hoopers, nosework, obedience, FCI Rally Obedience and dog dancing competitions with their entries, follow competitions and start a new club. Seminars, competition day and rules: handlers find seminars, sign dogs up by day or by group and read their entries, fees and group schedule; seminar organizers handle entries and build and publish groups; handlers read their dogs' start times, competition news and ZKwP ranking points; anyone asks rules questions answered with quoted rulebook passages, suggests a missing agility competition and browses courses from the course designer. Six more prompts guide these.
